description.value: A preliminary real-time fMRI neurofeedback study examined whether nicotine-dependent cigarette smokers could voluntarily reduce ACC activity and craving or increase mPFC activity while viewing smoking cues.

spans.text: In this study, we explored the feasibility of self-regulation of frontal cortical activation using real time fMRI (rtfMRI) neurofeedback in nicotine-dependent cigarette smokers during exposure to smoking cues.

value: we hypothesized that using rtfMRI neurofeedback smokers would decrease the BOLD signal in the ACC following instructions to “reduce craving” and increase the BOLD signal in middle prefrontal cortex following instructions to “increase resistance” to craving while viewing smoking-related cues in the scanner.

description.value: Participants viewed smoking-related and neutral cues while attempting to reduce craving or increase resistance to craving using real-time fMRI neurofeedback.

smoking-related
